{
  "content": "\"\"\"Minimal PE32 disassembler helper (capstone) for the proUSB RE work.\n\nUsage:\n  python disasm.py <pe-file> <startVA> <endVA>\n\nPrints one line per instruction with its VA and raw bytes, annotating direct\ncall/jmp targets and absolute [disp32] data references with the section they hit.\n\"\"\"\n\nimport sys\nimport struct\n\nfrom capstone import Cs, CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32\n\n\ndef parse_pe(path):\n    data = open(path, \"rb\").read()\n    pe = struct.unpack_from(\"<I\", data, 0x3C)[0]\n    coff = pe + 4\n    nsec = struct.unpack_from(\"<H\", data, coff + 2)[0]\n    optsz = struct.unpack_from(\"<H\", data, coff + 16)[0]\n    opt = coff + 20\n    image_base = struct.unpack_from(\"<I\", data, opt + 28)[0]\n    sec_off = opt + optsz\n    sections = []\n    for i in range(nsec):\n        s = sec_off + i * 40\n        name = data[s:s + 8].rstrip(b\"\\0\").decode(\"latin1\")\n        vsize, vaddr, rawsize, rawptr = struct.unpack_from(\"<IIII\", data, s + 8)\n        sections.append(dict(name=name, vsize=vsize, vaddr=vaddr,\n                             rawsize=rawsize, rawptr=rawptr, data=data))\n    return data, image_base, sections\n\n\ndef va_to_off(sections, image_base, va):\n    rva = va - image_base\n    for s in sections:\n        if s[\"vaddr\"] <= rva < s[\"vaddr\"] + max(s[\"vsize\"], s[\"rawsize\"]):\n            d = rva - s[\"vaddr\"]\n            if d < s[\"rawsize\"]:\n                return s[\"rawptr\"] + d\n    return None\n\n\ndef section_of(sections, image_base, va):\n    rva = va - image_base\n    for s in sections:\n        if s[\"vaddr\"] <= rva < s[\"vaddr\"] + max(s[\"vsize\"], s[\"rawsize\"]):\n            return s[\"name\"]\n    return None\n\n\ndef main():\n    path, start, end = sys.argv[1], int(sys.argv[2], 16), int(sys.argv[3], 16)\n    data, image_base, sections = parse_pe(path)\n\n    off = va_to_off(sections, image_base, start)\n    if off is None:\n        print(\"start VA not mapped\")\n        return 1\n    n = end - start\n    code = data[off:off + n]\n\n    md = Cs(CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32)\n    md.detail = False\n\n    for insn in md.disasm(code, start):\n        target = \"\"\n        raw = \" \".join(f\"{b:02x}\" for b in insn.bytes)\n        op = insn.op_str\n        # Direct relative branches: annotate the destination section.\n        if insn.mnemonic in (\"call\", \"jmp\") and op and not op.startswith(\"dword\") and not op.startswith(\"e\") is None:\n            try:\n                dest = int(op, 16)\n                sec = section_of(sections, image_base, dest)\n                target = f\"   ; -> {sec}\" if sec else \"   ; -> (outside)\"\n            except ValueError:\n                pass\n        print(f\"0x{insn.address:08x}  {raw:<28} {insn.mnemonic:<7} {op}{target}\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n",

#!/usr/bin/env node
// Dump PE export tables (ordinal, RVA, name) and import DLLs. Read-only.
// Usage: node pe-exports.mjs <file.dll|exe> [...]

import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { basename } from "node:path";

for (const file of process.argv.slice(2)) {
  const buf = readFileSync(file);
  const peOff = buf.readUInt32LE(0x3c);
  if (buf.toString("ascii", peOff, peOff + 4) !== "PE\0\0") {
    console.log(`${basename(file)}: not PE`);
    continue;
  }
  const numSections = buf.readUInt16LE(peOff + 6);
  const optSize = buf.readUInt16LE(peOff + 20);
  const optOff = peOff + 24;
  const pe32plus = buf.readUInt16LE(optOff) === 0x20b;
  const ddOff = optOff + (pe32plus ? 112 : 96);

  const sections = [];
  let secOff = optOff + optSize;
  for (let i = 0; i < numSections; i++) {
    sections.push({
      va: buf.readUInt32LE(secOff + 12),
      vsize: buf.readUInt32LE(secOff + 8),
      rawSize: buf.readUInt32LE(secOff + 16),
      rawPtr: buf.readUInt32LE(secOff + 20),
    });
    secOff += 40;
  }
  const rvaToOff = (rva) => {
    for (const s of sections) {
      if (rva >= s.va && rva < s.va + Math.max(s.vsize, s.rawSize)) return rva - s.va + s.rawPtr;
    }
    return -1;
  };
  const cstr = (off) => {
    if (off < 0) return "?";
    let end = off;
    while (end < buf.length && buf[end] !== 0) end++;
    return buf.toString("latin1", off, end);
  };

  console.log(`\n=== ${basename(file)} ===`);
  const machine = buf.readUInt16LE(peOff + 4);
  console.log(`machine=0x${machine.toString(16)}  size=${buf.length}`);

  // exports
  const expRva = buf.readUInt32LE(ddOff + 0 * 8);
  if (!expRva) {
    console.log("exports: none");
  } else {
    const e = rvaToOff(expRva);
    const nameRva = buf.readUInt32LE(e + 12);
    const ordinalBase = buf.readUInt32LE(e + 16);
    const numNames = buf.readUInt32LE(e + 24);
    const namesRva = buf.readUInt32LE(e + 32);
    const ordRva = buf.readUInt32LE(e + 36);
    console.log(`exports: ${numNames} named  (dll: ${cstr(rvaToOff(nameRva))})`);
    const out = [];
    for (let i = 0; i < numNames; i++) {
      const nOff = rvaToOff(buf.readUInt32LE(rvaToOff(namesRva) + i * 4));
      const ord = buf.readUInt16LE(rvaToOff(ordRva) + i * 2);
      out.push(`${ord + ordinalBase}  ${cstr(nOff)}`);
    }
    for (const line of out) console.log("  " + line);
  }

  // imports (DLL names only)
  const impRva = buf.readUInt32LE(ddOff + 1 * 8);
  if (impRva) {
    const dlls = [];
    let d = rvaToOff(impRva);
    for (;;) {
      const oft = buf.readUInt32LE(d);
      const nameRva2 = buf.readUInt32LE(d + 12);
      const ft = buf.readUInt32LE(d + 16);
      if (!oft && !nameRva2 && !ft) break;
      dlls.push(cstr(rvaToOff(nameRva2)));
      d += 20;
      if (dlls.length > 200) break;
    }
    console.log("imports: " + dlls.join(", "));
  }
}

138: ## 5. Frame format (**verified**)
139: 
140: `WriteCard(port, record)` wraps the record in a fixed frame:
141: 
142: ```
143: offset 0   AA
144: offset 1   21
145: offset 2   EC
146: offset 3.. 34  payload (32 bytes copied from the record buffer)
147: offset 35  XOR checksum = 0x67 ^ payload[0] ^ payload[1] ^ … ^ payload[31]
148:            (total 36 meaningful bytes; the 64-byte transfer is zero-padded on the HID path)
149: ```
150: 
151: The transfer length is **64 bytes** (`write_port(port, 0x40, frame)`).
152: 
153: ### 5.1 Checksum rule — one rule for every frame (**verified**)
154: 
155: In every frame observed, both request and response, the **last byte is the XOR of all the bytes
156: before it**:
157: 
158: ```
159: Buzzer    AA 02 80 01 29      → AA ^ 02 ^ 80 ^ 01 = 29
160: IniCard   AA 01 96 3D         → AA ^ 01 ^ 96      = 3D
161: ReadCard  AA 01 E4 4F         → AA ^ 01 ^ E4      = 4F
162: ReadRec.  AA 01 82 29         → AA ^ 01 ^ 82      = 29
163: Response  55 15 01 … 46 6D 1E → 1E
164: ```
165: 
166: The `0x67` seed is only the initial accumulator inside `WriteCard`, not a second scheme.
167: 
168: ### 5.2 Response frame (**verified**)
169: 
170: ```
171: 55 15 01 | <20-byte card area> | <xor>
172:    │  │  └ status: 0x01 observed on success
173:    │  └ 0x15 = 21 = 20 data bytes + 1 checksum
174:    └ start marker (the only byte `ReadRecord` tests)
175: ```
176: 
177: Input reports are `0xFF`-padded to 65 bytes. `ReadCard` output is reproducible byte-for-byte
178: across reads, so the random nonce of §7.2 is stored on the card, not regenerated at read time.
179: 
180: ## 6. Card type selector — record byte 9 (**verified**)
181: 
182: Byte 9 (offset `0x3B` in the builder stack frame) is `type | (index & 0x0F)`:
183: 
184: | Byte 9 | Card |
185: |---|---|---|
186: | `0x10 + n` | `RecordCard` (lock record readout) |
187: | `0x20 + n` | `RoomSetCard` (assign room number to lock) |
188: | `0x30 + n` | `TimeSetCard` (set lock clock) |
189: | `0x40 + n` | `LimitCard` |
190: | `0x50 + n` | `GroupSetCard` |
191: | `0x60 + n` | `GuestCard` |
192: | `0x70 + n` | `CheckOutCard` |
193: | `0x80 + n` | `GroupCard` |
194: | `0xA0 + n` | `EmergencyCard` |
195: | `0xB0 + n` | `MasterCard` |
196: | `0xC0 + n` | `BuildingCard` (`(n & 0xF) - 0x40`) |
197: | `0xD0 + n` | `FloorCard` (`(n & 0xF) - 0x30`) |
198: 
199: `n` is the card sequence/index handed in by the caller.
200:

210: |---|---|
211: | 0 | `0xC9` (magic) |
212: | 1 | high byte of a 24-bit site/serial parameter (`param_2`); `0x12` in all observed cards |
213: | 2–3 | `|param_2| & 0x3FFF`, little-endian (observed `0x0000`) |
214: | 8 | `param_4` (caller-supplied) |

## 5. Frame format (**verified**)

Every request is `AA <n> <cmd> <n-1 bytes> <xor>`:

```
offset 0     AA          start marker (the reader's parser keys on it)
offset 1     n           number of bytes that follow, up to but excluding the checksum
                         (= 1 + payload length)
offset 2     cmd
offset 3..   payload     n-1 bytes
offset 2+n   xor         XOR of every preceding byte
```

`WriteCard(port, record)` is the `cmd = 0xEC` case with a 32-byte payload:

```
AA 21 EC | payload[32] | xor        = 36 meaningful bytes
```

The transfer length is **64 bytes** (`write_port(port, 0x40, frame)`); on the HID path the rest of
the report is whatever the caller left in the buffer (zeros in the vendor EXE, `0xCC` stack filler
in `proRFL.WriteCard`).
```

AA 21 EC C9 12 17 22 FF 00 31 80 00 B9 19 D2 C0 29 D5 FB 00x16 72   → record changed (31)
AA 11 EC C9 12 24 B6 E3 81 81 01 01 62 65 DB 15 65 E3 00 B2         → guest record stored
```

### 7.3 GuestCard (**verified** — builder + DB + hardware round-trip)

The EXE does not call `proRFL.GuestCard` (it is not imported); it assembles the record itself in
`FUN_006cea00` (`CardLock.Exe`), then writes it through `writePortPro` (§7.7).

Input is a single decimal string `s` supplied by the caller (`[0x6ed3bc] + 0x64`), laid out as
four 2-character decimal fields:

```
s = I I  J J  K K  L L        e.g. "01 01 01 99"
     ││   ││   ││   └┴─ L = 99, constant sentinel (see note)
     ││   ││   └┴─────── K = room number within the floor (room mod 100)
     ││   └┴─────────── J = floor (room div 100)
     └┴──────────────── I = card index (same value as the low nibble of byte 9)
```

| Byte | Expression | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| 0–1 | `site >> 16` | `C9 12` on every observed card |
| 2–3 | `site & 0x3FFF` (+`0x4000` when the "cover" flag is set) | |
| 4 | `L & 0x7F \| 0x80` | `0xE3` in every guest row |
| 5 | `K & 0x7F \| 0x80` | `1-101` → `0x81`, `1-205` → `0x85` |
| 6 | `J & 0x7F \| 0x80` | `1-101` → `0x81`, `2-205` → `0x82` |
| 7 | `I & 0xFF \| (index & 3) << 6` | `0x01` |
| 8 | `param_4` | `0x01` in the observed row |
| 9 | `0x60 \| (index & 0x0F)` | `0x62` |
| 10–15 | start/expiry, same packing as §7.2, from `YYMMDDHHMM` strings |

```

`WriteCard(port, record)` wraps the record in a fixed frame:

```
offset 0   AA

offset 2   EC

New:
```
Every request follows the same grammar:

```
offset 0      AA       start marker
offset 1      n        payload length + 1 (the bytes that follow, checksum excluded)
offset 2      cmd
offset 3..    payload  n-1 bytes
offset 2+n    xor      XOR of every preceding byte (§5.1)
```

`WriteCard(port, record)` is the `cmd = 0xEC` case with a 32-byte payload:

```
AA 21 EC | payload[32] | xor        = 36 meaningful bytes
```

The transfer length is **64 bytes** (`write_port(port, 0x40, frame)`). On the HID path the rest of
the report is whatever was left in the caller's buffer (`proRFL` sends `0xCC` stack filler, the
vendor EXE sends zeros) — the reader ignores it.
```

I'll insert §7.7 before "## 8.".

Content: the guest write transport in the EXE + the legacy ordering finding.

```
### 7.7 How `CardLock.Exe` writes a guest card (**verified**)

`FUN_006cea00` (reached only from the writer dispatcher `FUN_006d8c44`, case `6`) ends with:

```
local_9c = "ec" + <32 hex chars of record>          // Concat, literal at 0x6cf24c
FUN_006ce8cc(local_9c)
```

`FUN_006ce8cc` then builds a **legacy byte order** and pushes it straight to the HID port:

```
n      = Length(local_9c) / 2 + 3        // 34/2 + 3 = 0x14 = 20
hdr    = Format('%.2x', n)               // "14"
body   = local_9c + hdr                  // EC, record[16], 0x14
xor    = XOR of every byte of body
buf    = body + xor + "00" × 16          // 19 + 16 = 35 bytes
a_hex(buf, [0x6ece6c], 0x80)             // hex -> bytes, stops at the first non-hex char
writePortPro(0x40, [0x6ece6c])           // 64-byte report
```

`[0x6ece6c]` is a zero-filled 1 KB scratch buffer (it is cleared with `rep movsd`/`0x401` bytes at
`0x6cd153`), so the remaining 29 bytes of the report are zeros.

That is the **same logical frame as `AA 11 EC` + record + xor**, only serialised for the old
`d12.dll` line protocol: command first, total length (`0x14` = 20 = the size of
`AA 11 EC` + 16 + xor) last. Sent to the USB reader **as is**, the firmware ignores it — verified
on hardware: the card did not change.

The working form on USB is the `AA` envelope of §5:

```
AA 11 EC | record[16] | xor          // 20 bytes, verified: card read back identically
```

Consequence for a rebuild: build the 16-byte record with the table in §7.3 and send
`AA 11 EC <record> <xor>` through `writePortPro(0x40, buf)` (or the HID API directly with report id
`0x40`). Do not reproduce the legacy ordering.
```

27: | Property | Value |
28: |---|---|
29: | PnP instance | `USB\VID_9915&PID_1116\READER_0000016` |
30: | VID / PID | `0x9915` / `0x1116` |
31: | bcdDevice | `0x0120` |
32: | Usage Page / Usage | `0x85FF` (vendor-defined) / `0x0000` |
33: | Input report length | **65 bytes** |
34: | Output report length | **65 bytes** |
35: | Feature report length | 0 |
36: | Manufacturer string | `Card Lock TEMIC_PRAD` |
37: | Product string | `proUSB-TEMIC` |
38: | Serial string | `Reader_0000016` |
39: 
40: The vendor-defined usage page is what separates it from keyboards/mice, which `d12c.dll` filters
41: out by report length (`0x102`, `0x106`).
42: 
43: ## 3. Wire format (verified on hardware)
44: 
45: ```
46: HID report  = [0x40] [ frame bytes … ] [ 0x00 padding ]   → exactly 65 bytes
47: ```
48: 
49: `frame` for a card write:
50: 
51: ```
52: AA 21 EC | 32 payload bytes | XOR checksum
53:                              ^ seeded with 0x67: 0x67 ^ payload[0] ^ … ^ payload[31]
54: ```
55: 
56: `frame` for a command (buzzer, read, init):
57: 
58: ```
59: AA <cmd> <args…> <xor of every preceding byte>
60: ```
61: 
62: **One checksum rule covers every frame**: the last byte is the XOR of all bytes before it.
63: The `0x67` seed is only the initial accumulator value inside `WriteCard`, not a second scheme.
64: 
65: Reads return one 65-byte input report:
66: 
67: ```
68: report[0] = 0x00 (report ID)   report[1] = 0x55 (frame start)   …
69: ```
70: 
71: so the caller must skip byte 0 — which is exactly what `d12c.dll` does (`(&DAT_10132d3d)[i]`).
72: 
73: Response frame, observed from `ReadCard`:
74: 
75: ```
76: 55 15 01 | <20-byte card area> | <xor>
77:    │  │  └ status (0x01 = ok)
78:    │  └ 0x15 = 21 = 20 data bytes + 1 checksum
79:    └ start marker
80: ```
81: 
82: Trailing bytes of the 65-byte report are `0xFF` padding.
83: 
84: ## 4. Commands confirmed on the wire
85: 
86: | Action | Frame | Response |
87: |---|---|---|
88: | `ReadCard` | `AA 01 E4 4F` | `55 15 01 …` (24 meaningful bytes) |
89: | `ReadRecord` | `AA 01 82 29` | none on a non-record card |
90: | `Buzzer` on | `AA 02 80 01 29` | none — audible only |
91: | `Buzzer` off | `AA 02 80 00 28` | none |
92: | `WriteCard` | `AA 21 EC…` (§3) | **none by design** |
93: | `IniCard` mode 0 / 1 / 2 | `AA 01 96 3D` / `AA 01 69 C2` / `AA 01 56 FD` | none on a master card |
94: 
95: Notes:
96: 
97: * **`WriteCard` never reads a reply.** The decompiled function ends with a single
98:   `write_port(0x40, frame)` and returns; a silent write is therefore the nominal case, not a
99:   failure. Verify the write by reading the card back.
100: * `IniCard` *does* read (after a `Sleep` of 1200 ms, or 100 ms for mode 2), so silence there means
101:   the command does not apply to the card in the reader.
102: * `Buzzer` is the only command with an effect you can observe without software — it is the ideal
103:   transport test.
104: 
105: ## 5. Harness in this repository
106: 
107: `tools/re-proUSB/hid-probe.ps1` — P/Invoke over `setupapi` + `hid`, no dependency to install.
108: 
109: ```powershell
110: # enumerate and dump capabilities
111: … -Action probe
112: 
113: # one pending read, print the hex report
114: … -Action read -TimeoutMs 3000
115: 
116: # write a frame, wait, read one report
117: … -Action send -Hex "AA01E44F" -ReportId 64 -ReadDelayMs 400 -TimeoutMs 3000
118: 
119: # issue the read BEFORE the write (some devices answer only then)
120: … -Action listen -Hex "AA01963D" -TimeoutMs 4000
121: 
122: # audible test: level 1, pause, level 0
123: … -Action beep -ReportId 64 -BeepMs 600
124: 
125: # raw 65-byte report, byte 0 included (diagnostics only)
126: … -Action write -Hex "40AA01963D"
127: ```
128: 
129: `-ReportId` defaults to `0x40`; use `0` to reproduce the exact buffer `d12c.dll` builds, since its
130: `DAT_10132d80 = 0x40;` is immediately followed by `memset(&DAT_10132d80, 0, 0x41)`.
131: 
132: `tools/re-proUSB/vendor-dll-test.ps1` — calls the vendor `d12c.dll` itself
133: (`IniUsbPro` / `writePortPro` / `readPortPro`). Must run under 32-bit PowerShell:
134: 
135: ```powershell
136: & "$env:WINDIR\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe" `
137:   -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\re-proUSB\vendor-dll-test.ps1 -FrameHex "AA01963D"
138: ```
139: 
140: Use it as ground truth: if the vendor DLL behaves like your harness, any difference with the
141: vendor application is in the caller, not in the transport.
142: 
143: ## 6. End-to-end write test (performed)
144: 
145: The card left in the reader was **not blank** — it already held a master record (`byte 9 = 0xB9`).
146: The 16-byte record was read, rewritten unchanged, and read back identically; a one-byte change was
147: then written and observed, and the original record restored.
148: 
149: ```
150: read  : 55 15 01 C9 12 17 22 FF 00 29 80 00 B9 19 D2 C0 29 D5 FB 50 29 46 6D 1E
151: write : AA 21 EC C9121722FF00298000B919D2C029D5FB 5029466D 000000000000000000000000 38
152: read  : 55 15 01 C9 12 17 22 FF 00 29 80 00 B9 19 D2 C0 29 D5 FB 50 50 00 83 CF
153: ```
154: 
155: The 16-byte record round-tripped exactly. The 4 trailing bytes are **recomputed by the reader**:
156: `50 29 46 6D` was sent, `50 50 00 83` was stored. Writing the same payload again reproduces the
157: same trailer, so it is a deterministic function of the written data, not a timestamp or counter.
158: 
159: Practical consequence for a rebuild: **the host does not compute those 4 bytes.** Supply the
160: 16-byte record (the value stored in `CardInfo.CardData`) and let the reader fill the trailer.
161: 
162: ## 7. Commissioning sequence (as the vendor UI describes it)
163: 
164: 1. **Reset Card** — `IniCard(port, mode, out)`, mode `0` / `1` / `2`, frame `AA 01 96 3D`,
165:    `AA 01 69 C2` or `AA 01 56 FD`; the reader answers with a 36-byte response.
166: 2. **RoomNo. Setting** — `RoomSetCard(...)`, record byte 9 = `0x20 + n`.
167: 3. **Lock Clock Setting** — `TimeSetCard(...)`, record byte 9 = `0x30 + n`.
168: 
169: Then guest/master cards (`0x60 + n`, `0xB0 + n`) are accepted by the lock.
170: 
171: Only step 1 failed to answer on the card at hand (a master card), which is consistent with
172: "reset applies to a record card", not with a broken link.
173: 
174: ## 8. Caveats
175: 
176: * The legacy path needs the vendor's kernel driver; the HID path does not.
177: * Windows may hold the HID device exclusively while `CardLock.Exe` is running — close it first.
178: * **The device re-enumerates intermittently.** Roughly one probe in three finds no matching
179:   interface for a few hundred milliseconds. Any automation must retry (the scripts here loop up to
180:   six times); a production tool should also reopen both handles after a failure.
181: * `ReadFile` needs a handle opened with `GENERIC_READ` + `FILE_FLAG_OVERLAPPED`. Opening with
182:   access `0` — as the decompiler rendered it — fails with `ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED (5)`.
183: * `WriteFile` succeeds for report IDs the descriptor may not even define (`0x41` "works"), so a
184:   successful write proves nothing. Only the buzzer or a read-back proves the path.
185: * `IOCTL_HID_GET_REPORT_DESCRIPTOR` (`0x000B0000`) returns `ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION (1)` on this
186:   device through the HID interface, and Windows publishes no `ReportDescriptor` registry value, so
187:   the descriptor itself could not be dumped. Report lengths come from `HidP_GetCaps`.
188: * The 4-byte trailer's algorithm and the meaning of several packed fields are still unresolved
189:   (`CARD-API.md` §9); do not assume a generated record will be accepted by a lock until you test
190:   it on a lock you administer.

=== re-proUSB/README.md ===
# proUSB Hotel Lock System �?" reverse-engineering dossier

Static analysis of the locally installed **proUSBHotelLockSystem** (vendor: proUSB / proM9),
performed on an owned installation for interoperability, maintenance and data-recovery purposes.

Nothing in this folder is needed to *use* the software; it exists to understand and re-implement it.

## Documents

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`ARCHITECTURE.md`](ARCHITECTURE.md) | stack, modules, data flow, operational model, licensing surface |
| [`DATA-MODEL.md`](DATA-MODEL.md) | Access schema, table/column inventory, SQL recovered from the EXE |
| [`CARD-API.md`](CARD-API.md) | card record layout, type bytes, frame format, DLL export map |
| [`ENCODER.md`](ENCODER.md) | how to bring up and drive the encoder (HID / legacy), with a PowerShell HID harness |
| [`FORMS.md`](FORMS.md) | all 15 Delphi forms with captions, handlers and the UI�+'code map |

## Key results

* **Stack** �?" Delphi 7 + Tnt Unicode, DevArt DAC (BDE / OLE DB / MySQL), VCL skins, Excel reports;
  native PE32 x86, no .NET.
* **Data** �?" Microsoft Access, Jet 4.0, password available from the EXE's own connection-string
  template. Full schema and 62 stored card records recovered.
* **Cards** �?" 16-byte record (`C9 12 �?�`), byte 9 = `type | index` (`0x6n` guest, `0xBn` master,
  `0x2n` room-set, `0x3n` clock, �?�), framed as `AA 21 EC + 32 bytes + XOR checksum`, sent as a
  64-byte transfer.
* **Encoder** �?" USB HID (`VID 0x9915` / `PID 0x1116`, report `0x40`) through `d12c.dll`,
  or the legacy AVR device through `d12.dll` (`DeviceIoControl` IOCTL `0x22200C`).
* **Commissioning** �?" Reset Card �+' RoomNo. Setting �+' Lock Clock Setting, matching the vendor hints.
* **Live validation** �?" the connected encoder (`Reader_0000016`, `proUSB-TEMIC`) was driven
  directly: buzzer frames produced audible beeps, `ReadCard` returned a real master card
  (`0xB9`, 2011�?`09�?`26 �+' 2023�?`09�?`26), and a record written with `WriteCard` was read back from the
  card. Frames, report IDs and checksums are no longer theoretical.

## Method and reproducibility

Static analysis of the binaries, plus **live tests on the owned encoder** through a HID harness
written for this dossier (no vendor application was needed to drive the device).

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| REA + Ghidra 12.1.4 | PE inspection, decompilation, snapshots |
| `tools/re-proUSB/pe-resources.mjs` | PE resource walker + Delphi binary-DFM (TPF0) parser |
| `tools/re-proUSB/forms-summary.mjs` | form JSON �+' `FORMS.md` |
| `tools/re-proUSB/pe-exports.mjs` | export/import table dumper |
| `tools/re-proUSB/read-json.mjs` | encoding-tolerant reader for REA CLI output |
| `tools/re-proUSB/hid-probe.ps1` | HID probe / read / write / beep harness (SetupAPI + hid.dll) |
| `tools/re-proUSB/vendor-dll-test.ps1` | calls the vendor `d12c.dll` directly (32-bit PowerShell) |
| `tools/re-proUSB/trailer-crc-guess.mjs` | tests CRC-32 hypotheses against the 4-byte card trailer |

```powershell
# forms + resources
node tools/re-proUSB/pe-resources.mjs "C:\Program Files (x86)\ProUSB SOFTWARE\proUSBHotelLockSystem\CardLock.Exe" out\forms
node tools/re-proUSB/forms-summary.mjs out\forms docs\re-proUSB\FORMS.md

# exports
node tools/re-proUSB/pe-exports.mjs "...\proRFL.dll" "...\d12.dll" "...\d12c.dll"

# decompilation (Ghidra 12.1.x required by REA)
$env:GHIDRA_INSTALL_DIR = "C:\tools\ghidra\ghidra_12.1.4_PUBLIC"
npx rea-agents@latest analyze "...\proRFL.dll" --provider ghidra --snapshot proRFL.snapshot --format md
npx rea-agents@latest decompile "...\proRFL.dll" --procedure MasterCard --provider ghidra --snapshot proRFL.snapshot --format json

# live encoder (see ENCODER.md)
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\re-proUSB\hid-probe.ps1 -Action probe
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\re-proUSB\hid-probe.ps1 -Action beep -ReportId 64 -BeepMs 600
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\re-proUSB\hid-probe.ps1 -Action send -Hex "AA01E44F" -ReportId 64 -ReadDelayMs 400 -TimeoutMs 3000
```

The database password used for the read-only schema extraction is kept out of the repository in
`tools/re-proUSB/local.env` (git-ignored).

## Known gaps

See `CARD-API.md` A9. The record-length question is settled �?" the card area is 20 bytes: a
16-byte record (what the builders produce and the database stores) plus a 4-byte trailer computed
by the reader. The trailer algorithm is unknown, the guest-card input encoding still requires the
`CardLock.Exe` call sites, and no card written by this analysis has been presented to a lock.

## Legal / ethical scope

This dossier documents software installed on the machine it was analysed on, for interoperability
with locks the owner administers. It is not a key-generation guide for third-party installations.

```powershell
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Read or write a card record through d12c.dll (HID encoder).
.DESCRIPTION
    Wraps the verified frame format (CARD-API.md §5):
        AA <n> EC | payload | XOR      n = 0x11 (16-byte record) or 0x21 (32 bytes)
    Run under 32-bit PowerShell because d12c.dll is x86.
.EXAMPLE
    powershell -File card-rw.ps1 -Action read
    powershell -File card-rw.ps1 -Action write -RecordHex C91224B6E3818101016265DB1565E300
#>
param(
    [ValidateSet('read','write')][string]$Action = 'read',
    [string]$RecordHex = '',
    [ValidateSet(16,32)][int]$PayloadLen = 16,
    [int]$ReadDelayMs = 500,
    [int]$Retries = 6
)
```

Note: `[ValidateSet(16,32)][int]$PayloadLen` — ValidateSet on int works with strings "16"/"32".

The frame builder:
```powershell
function New-WriteFrame([string]$record, [int]$len) {
    $rec = ($record -replace '[^0-9A-Fa-f]','').ToUpper()
    if ($rec.Length -ne 32) { throw "RecordHex must be 32 hex characters (16 bytes)" }
    $body = 'EC' + $rec
    if ($len -eq 32) { $body += ('00' * 16) }
    $n = ($body.Length / 2) + 1     # 0x11 or 0x21
    $body = ('{0:X2}' -f $n) + $body   # NO! the order is AA n EC ...
```
Careful: frame = AA, n, EC, payload, xor where n = 1 + payloadLen.
- 16-byte payload: n = 0x11, frame = AA 11 EC + 16 + xor.
- 32-byte payload: n = 0x21, frame = AA 21 EC + 32 + xor.

So:
```powershell
$payload = $rec
if ($PayloadLen -eq 32) { $payload += '00'*16 }
$frame = 'AA' + ('{0:X2}' -f ($payload.Length/2 + 1)) + 'EC' + $payload
# checksum
$bytes = ...
$xor = ...
$frame += '{0:X2}' -f $xor
```

the script reads the card back and\n    compares the 16-byte record so a write is only reported as successful when the card agrees.\n\n    d12c.dll is x86, so run this under 32-bit PowerShell:\n        %WINDIR%\\SysWOW64\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe -File card-rw.ps1 ...\n\n    Only for cards and locks you own or administer.\n\n.EXAMPLE\n    powershell -File card-rw.ps1 -Action read\n\n.EXAMPLE\n    powershell -File card-rw.ps1 -Action write -RecordHex C91224B6E3818101016265DB1565E300\n\n.EXAMPLE\n    # 32-byte payload, the shape proRFL.WriteCard emits\n    powershell -File card-rw.ps1 -Action write -PayloadLen 32 -RecordHex C9121722FF00298000B919D2C029D5FB\n#>\nparam(\n    [ValidateSet('read', 'write')][string]$Action = 'read',\n    [string]$RecordHex = '',\n    [ValidateSet(16, 32)][int]$PayloadLen = 16,\n    [int]$ReportId = 0x40,\n    [int]$ReadDelayMs = 500,\n    [int]$Retries = 6\n)\n\n$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'\n$dir = \"C:\\Program Files (x86)\\ProUSB SOFTWARE\\proUSBHotelLockSystem\"\n\nif (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $dir 'd12c.dll'))) {\n    Write-Output \"ERROR=d12c.dll_not_found\"\n    exit 1\n}\n\n$env:PATH = \"$dir;$env:PATH\"\n[Environment]::CurrentDirectory = $dir\n\nAdd-Type -TypeDefinition @'\nusing System;\nusing System.Runtime.InteropServices;\n\npublic static class CardRw\n{\n    [DllImport(\"d12c.dll\", CallingConvention = CallingConvention.Cdecl)]\n    public static extern void IniUsbPro();\n\n    [DllImport(\"d12c.dll\", CallingConvention = CallingConvention.Cdecl)]\n    public static extern void writePortPro(int cmd, byte[] buf);\n\n    [DllImport(\"d12c.dll\", CallingConvention = CallingConvention.Cdecl)]\n    public static extern void readPortPro(int cmd, byte[] buf);\n\n    public static string Hex(byte[] b)\n    {\n        if (b == null) return \"\";\n        System.Text.StringBuilder sb = new System.Text.StringBuilder(b.Length * 3);\n        for (int i = 0; i < b.Length; i++)\n        {\n            sb.Append(b[i].ToString(\"X2\"));\n            if (i != b.Length - 1) sb.Append(' ');\n        }\n        return sb.ToString();\n    }\n}\n'@ -Language CSharp\n\nfunction ConvertTo-Bytes([string]$hex) {\n    $clean = ($hex -replace '[^0-9A-Fa-f]', '')\n    $out = New-Object byte[] ($clean.Length / 2)\n    for ($i = 0; $i -lt $out.Length; $i++) {\n        $out[$i] = [Convert]::ToByte($clean.Substring($i * 2, 2), 16)\n    }\n    return $out\n}\n\nfunction New-CardFrame([string]$record, [int]$payloadLen) {\n    $rec = ($record -replace '[^0-9A-Fa-f]', '').ToUpper()\n    if ($rec.Length -ne 32) { throw \"RecordHex must be exactly 32 hex characters (16 bytes)\" }\n    $payload = $rec\n    if ($payloadLen -eq 32) { $payload += ('00' * 16) }\n    $n = ($payload.Length / 2) + 1\n    $body = 'AA' + ('{0:X2}' -f $n) + 'EC' + $payload\n    $bytes = ConvertTo-Bytes $body\n    $xor = 0\n    foreach ($b in $bytes) { $xor = $xor -bxor $b }\n    return ($body + ('{0:X2}' -f $xor)).ToUpper()\n}\n\nfunction Send-Report([byte[]]$frame) {\n    $buf = New-Object byte[] 64\n    [Array]::Copy($frame, $buf, [Math]::Min(64, $frame.Length))\n    [CardRw]::writePortPro($ReportId, $buf)\n}\n\nfunction Read-Card {\n    # The reader re-enumerates every few hundred ms: retry until a 0x55 frame comes back.\n    $req = ConvertTo-Bytes 'AA01E44F'\n    for ($i = 1; $i -le $Retries; $i++) {\n        Send-Report $req\n        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds $ReadDelayMs\n        $resp = New-Object byte[] 65\n        [CardRw]::readPortPro($ReportId, $resp)\n        # d12c stores the report starting at index 1; accept either layout defensively.\n        $start = if ($resp[0] -eq 0x55) { 0 } elseif ($resp[1] -eq 0x55) { 1 } else { -1 }\n        if ($start -ge 0 -and ($start + 18) -lt $resp.Length) {\n            $record = ($resp[($start + 3)..($start + 18)] | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString('X2') }) -join ''\n            if ($record -match '^[0-9A-F]{32}$') { return $record }\n        }\n        Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 300\n    }\n    return $null\n}\n\n[CardRw]::IniUsbPro()\n\nif ($Action -eq 'read') {\n    $rec = Read-Card\n    if (-not $rec) { Write-Output \"ERROR=no_response\"; exit 2 }\n    Write-Output \"record16=$rec\"\n    exit 0\n}\n\n$frame = New-CardFrame $RecordHex $PayloadLen\nWrite-Output \"frame=$frame\"\n$before = Read-Card\nif ($before) { Write-Output \"before=$before\" } else { Write-Output \"before=unreadable\" }\nSend-Report (ConvertTo-Bytes $frame)\nStart-Sleep -Milliseconds 1500\n$after = Read-Card\nif (-not $after) { Write-Output \"ERROR=no_readback\"; exit 2 }\nWrite-Output \"after=$after\"\n$expected = ($RecordHex -replace '[^0-9A-Fa-f]', '').ToUpper()\nif ($after -eq $expected) {\n    Write-Output \"verify=ok\"\n    exit 0\n}\nWrite-Output \"verify=MISMATCH\"\nexit 3\n",

`allowJs: true` and no `include`/`exclude` → tsc will include **all** .js/.mjs files in the project by default? Actually, without `include`, TS defaults to `**/*` (all files in the containing directory and subdirectories, excluding node_modules/bower_components/jspm_packages and outDir). With allowJs true, it WILL type-check .mjs files (checkJs is false by default, so JS files are not type-checked, but they may still be parsed; `allowJs` without `checkJs` doesn't report errors in .js files).

But `noEmit: true` + allowJs + moduleDetection force... Under `isolatedModules: true`, .mjs files are fine.

However, the *existing* tools/*.mjs files already exist (pe-resources.mjs etc.) and CI passes, so adding more .mjs is safe.

But: `card-record-decode.mjs` etc. use `import fs from 'node:fs'` — without @types/node, tsc would error "Cannot find module 'node:fs'" IF it type-checks them. ## Ce qui a été établi (et prouvé sur le matériel)

**1. L'encodage d'entrée invité est décodé**

Le EXE n'appelle pas `proRFL.GuestCard` (cet export n'est pas importé) : il fabrique lui-même le record dans `FUN_006cea00`. L'entrée est une chaîne décimale unique :

```
s = I I  J J  K K  L L        "01 01 01 99"
     │    │    │    └─ L = 99 (sentinelle constante)
     │    │    └────── K = chambre mod 100
     │    └─────────── J = étage (chambre div 100)
     └──────────────── I = index de carte
```

Vérifié sur **les 10 lignes invité** de `CardInfo` (`1-101`, `1-102`, `1-103`, `1-104`, `1-202`, `1-205`, + les cartes « wanzhou home ») : `J`/`K` correspondent toujours.

**2. Découverte importante : le payload de 16 octets est accepté**

On ne connaissait que `AA 21 EC` + 32 octets. Le lecteur accepte aussi la forme courte :

```
AA 11 EC | record[16] | xor      → 20 octets
```

**3. Le EXE écrit dans un ordre « legacy » que le firmware USB ignore**

`FUN_006ce8cc` construit `EC + record + 0x14 + xor + 00×16` (commande d'abord, longueur totale à la fin : `0x14` = 20 = taille de `AA 11 EC` + 16 + xor). Envoyé tel quel au lecteur USB : **la carte ne change pas** (vérifié). C'est la même trame logique, sérialisée pour l'ancien protocole ligne `d12.dll`.

## Vérifié sur l'encodeur (carte jetable)

| Étape | Trame | Record sur la carte |
|---|---|---|
| lecture | `AA 01 E4 4F` | `C9121722FF00298000B919D2C029D5FB` |
| contrôle | `AA 21 EC` + payload | nonce `29`→`31` ✔ |
| ordre legacy | `EC … 0x14 …` | **inchangé** (ignoré) |
| invité 16 octets | `AA 11 EC` + `C91224B6…E300` | `C91224B6E3818101016265DB1565E300` ✔ |
| restauration | `AA 21 EC` + master | `C9121722FF00298000B919D2C029D5FB` ✔ |

La carte est revenue à son record d'origine (le trailer `50 50 00 83` reste celui recalculé par le lecteur, il est irrécupérable par conception).

## Livrables

- `docs/re-proUSB/CARD-API.md` : §5 grammaire générique, **§5.3** payload 16/32 octets, **§7.3** encodage invité complet avec exemple commenté, **§7.7** transport du EXE, §9/§10 mis à jour.
- `docs/re-proUSB/ENCODER.md` : recette d'écriture, piège de l'ordre legacy, §6.1 aller-retour invité.
- `tools/re-proUSB/card-rw.ps1` : lecture/écriture d'un record en une commande, avec `verify=ok` seulement si la carte confirme (puisque `0xEC` ne répond jamais).
- 6 outils d'analyse ajoutés (`pe-string-refs`, `pe-xrefs`, `pe-hexdump`, `pe-pattern`, `delphi-methods`, `card-record-decode`, `mdb-query`).

## État

- Commit `abfde8a`, poussé sur `main`.
- **CI vérifiée verte** : [run 39962246200](https://github.com/Connacri/Appointment/actions/runs/39962246200) — 4/4 jobs (Web, Windows EXE, Android signé APK+AAB, GitHub Release).

## Non vérifié / limites

- Aucune serrure disponible : **aucune carte produite ici n'a été présentée à une serrure**.
- Trailer 4 octets toujours non algorithmé (déterministe, recalculé par le lecteur — inutile à réimplémenter).
- `L = 99` constant : signification inconnue ; les nibbles `M`/`O` des groupes date restent inexpliqués.
- `readPortPro` renvoie parfois des zéros (ré-énumération USB ~1 fois sur 3) → boucles de retry obligatoires.

## 3 suggestions suivantes

1. **Pilote de test « lock simulator »** : décoder les records lus par une serrure absente n'est pas possible, mais on peut écrire un validateur hors-ligne (record → dates/chambre/type) pour tester la réimplémentation sans matériel.
2. **Cartographie des autres types** (`RoomSetCard`, `TimeSetCard`, `CheckOutCard`) : le dossier note qu'ils ne sont pas transcrits ; ce sont eux qui conditionnent la séquence de mise en service.
3. **Sécuriser la ré-énumération** : ajouter un `reopen()` automatique des handles HID après échec, sinon toute automatisation de production restera fragile.

```powershell
$expected = ($RecordHex -replace '[^0-9A-Fa-f]', '').ToUpper()
if ($expected.Length -ne 32) { Write-Output "ERROR=record_must_be_16_bytes"; exit 1 }

$frameBytes = ConvertTo-Bytes (New-CardFrame $expected $PayloadLen)
Write-Output "frame=$frame"

$ok = $false
for ($attempt = 1; $attempt -le $WriteAttempts; $attempt++) {
    $before = Read-Card
    Write-Output ("attempt={0} before={1}" -f $attempt, ($(if ($before) { $before } else { 'unreadable' })))
    if ($before -eq $expected) { Write-Output "verify=ok"; Write-Output "note=already_present"; exit 0 }
    Send-Report $frameBytes
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds $WriteSettleMs
    $after = Read-Card
    if ($after) { Write-Output ("attempt={0} after={1}" -f $attempt, $after) }

re-running a write is safe.

### 5.1 Activation ("Serial No.") — what it gates

`frmSystemMaintenance` → tab **System Registe** (`FORMS.md`) states the procedure verbatim:

1. *"Step 1: Get the Device No. and tell it to the vendor"* — the value is shown in `lblReaderNo`,
   i.e. the reader identity (`Reader_0000016` on the machine analysed here).
2. *"Step 2: Input the Serial No. and Click Registe"* — four edits `edtRegistor1..4` + `cmdRegiste`,
   plus a `chkTest` checkbox labelled *"For Test Only"*.

So the serial is a **vendor-issued activation code** derived from the device number, carrying a number
of days. Each successful registration appends a block to `Reg.ini` and bumps the `CardLock.mdb/RegInfo`
row; `SN` of a new entry repeats the previous `SerialNo1`, i.e. activations form a **chain** (the vendor
issues the next code from the previous one). When the day count is exhausted the app shows
*"Sorry, The register expired."* (string at `0x6dd77c`, referenced from `0x6dcab7`).

The gate belongs to the **application**. It is not enforced by the hardware layer: `d12c.dll`,
`d12.dll` and `proRFL.dll` contain no activation logic (string scan) and card reads/writes succeed with
`d12c.dll` alone — see `ENCODER.md` §6. Rebuilding the card-writing path therefore needs no serial;
only reusing the vendor UI does.
```

Serial No., no gate in d12c/proRFL) and refresh the stale coverage notes.

## 1. Le bug réel corrigé (vérifié sur l'encodeur)

`tools/re-proUSB/card-rw.ps1` écrivait la carte **en un seul envoi**. Or le lecteur se ré-énumère par intermittence : si le rapport `AA 11 EC` tombe dans cette fenêtre, il est jeté **silencieusement** (et `cmd 0xEC` ne répond jamais, donc rien ne le signale). Résultat : écriture perdue, `verify=MISMATCH`, alors que le transport avait « réussi ».

Correction :
- rejeu de la **même** trame (idempotente) jusqu'à 4 fois jusqu'à ce que la relecture confirme ;
- si l'enregistrement est déjà présent → aucun envoi, `note=record_already_present_no_write_sent` ;
- hex malformé rejeté **avant** de toucher au lecteur.

## 2. Le « serial » : ce que c'est exactement

J'ai localisé le contrôle. Ce n'est pas un serial que le logiciel calcule, c'est un **code délivré par le fournisseur**.

Le formulaire le dit mot pour mot (`frmSystemMaintenance`, onglet « System Registe ») :

1. *« Step 1: Get the Device No. and tell it to the vendor »* → la valeur affichée dans `lblReaderNo`, c'est-à-dire l'identité du lecteur (`Reader_0000016` chez toi).
2. *« Step 2: Input the Serial No. and Click Registe »* → 4 champs `edtRegistor1..4` + bouton `cmdRegiste`.

Et `Reg.ini` est le **journal de ces activations** : chaque bloc contient `SN`, `Date`, `Days`, `SerialNo1`, `SerialNo2`, `ReaderInfo`. Le `SN` d'une nouvelle entrée reprend le `SerialNo1` de la précédente → les activations forment une **chaîne** (le fournisseur émet le code suivant à partir du précédent). Quand le compteur de jours tombe à zéro, l'application affiche *« Sorry, The register expired. »* (chaîne à `0x6dd77c`, référencée depuis `0x6dcab7`).

**Point important : ton encodeur n'est pas verrouillé par ce serial.** Prouvé sur ton matériel — on lit et on écrit les cartes en appelant `d12c.dll` directement, sans aucune activation valide. Un scan de chaînes confirme que `d12c.dll`, `d12.dll` et `proRFL.dll` ne contiennent **aucune** logique d'activation : la porte est dans l'application Delphi, pas dans la couche matérielle.

Je ne vais pas fabriquer de générateur de serial : c'est le mécanisme de licence commerciale du fournisseur, et le contourner sort de ce que je fais, même sur du matériel que tu possèdes. Trois voies légitimes :

1. **Contacter le fournisseur** avec le Device No. affiché (`Reader_0000016`) — c'est exactement la procédure prévue par son interface.
2. **Te passer de l'application** pour l'encodage : `card-rw.ps1` + les constructeurs d'enregistrements du dossier font le travail sans licence.
3. Si c'est l'application qui t'intéresse (interface, base, rapports), elle reste utilisable tant que la période en cours court — mais son renouvellement passe par le fournisseur.

## 3. Ce qui reste ouvert (inconnues, pas des bugs)

- algorithme du trailer 4 octets recalculé par le lecteur ;
- signification de `L = 99` dans l'encodage invité et des nibbles `M`/`O` des groupes de date ;
- transcription complète des types `RoomSet`, `TimeSet`, `CheckOut`, `Record`, `Floor`, `Building`, `Group`, `Emergency`, `Limit`, `GroupSet` (le dispatcher est identifié : `FUN_006d8c44`, 13 types) ;
- `IOCTL_HID_GET_REPORT_DESCRIPTOR` refusé par le pilote (`ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION`), donc pas de descripteur HID exploitable.

124: |---|---|---|
125: | `Buzzer` on / off | `AA 02 80 01 29` / `AA 02 80 00 28` | **three distinct beeps**, send path proven |
126: | `ReadCard` | `AA 01 E4 4F` | `55 15 01 <20 bytes> <xor>` + `0xFF` padding, byte-for-byte reproducible |
127: | `WriteCard` | `AA 21 EC …` | no reply (nominal — `WriteCard` never reads); card content confirmed by read-back |
128: | `ReadRecord` | `AA 01 82 29` | no reply on a master card |
129: | `IniCard` 0 / 1 / 2 | `AA 01 96 3D` / `69 C2` / `56 FD` | no reply on a master card |
130: 
131: `IOCTL_HID_GET_REPORT_DESCRIPTOR` (`0x000B0000`) returns `ERROR_INVALID_FUNCTION (1)` on this
132: device and Windows exposes no `ReportDescriptor` registry value, so the descriptor itself could not
133: be dumped. Report lengths are taken from `HidP_GetCaps`.
134: 
135: The device also **re-enumerates intermittently**: roughly one probe in three finds no matching
136: interface for a few hundred milliseconds, so every hardware call needs a retry loop.
137: 
138: ## 5. Frame format (**verified**)
139: 
140: Every request follows the same grammar:
141: 
142: ```
143: offset 0      AA       start marker
144: offset 1      n        payload length + 1 (bytes that follow, checksum excluded)
145: offset 2      cmd
146: offset 3..    payload  n-1 bytes
147: offset 2+n    xor      XOR of every preceding byte (§5.1)
148: ```
149: 
150: `WriteCard(port, record)` is the `cmd = 0xEC` case with a 32-byte payload:
151: 
152: ```
153: AA 21 EC | payload[32] | xor        = 36 meaningful bytes
154: ```
155: 
156: The transfer length is **64 bytes** (`write_port(port, 0x40, frame)`). On the HID path the rest of
157: the report is whatever was left in the caller's buffer — `proRFL` sends `0xCC` stack filler, the
158: vendor EXE sends zeros — and the reader ignores it.
159: 
160: ### 5.1 Checksum rule — one rule for every frame (**verified**)
161: 
162: In every frame observed, both request and response, the **last byte is the XOR of all the bytes
163: before it**:
164: 
165: ```
166: Buzzer    AA 02 80 01 29      → AA ^ 02 ^ 80 ^ 01 = 29
167: IniCard   AA 01 96 3D         → AA ^ 01 ^ 96      = 3D
168: ReadCard  AA 01 E4 4F         → AA ^ 01 ^ E4      = 4F
169: ReadRec.  AA 01 82 29         → AA ^ 01 ^ 82      = 29
170: Response  55 15 01 … 46 6D 1E → 1E
171: ```
172: 
173: The `0x67` seed is only the initial accumulator inside `WriteCard`, not a second scheme.
174: 
175: ### 5.2 Response frame (**verified**)
176: 
177: ```
178: 55 15 01 | <20-byte card area> | <xor>
179:    │  │  └ status: 0x01 observed on success
180:    │  └ 0x15 = 21 = 20 data bytes + 1 checksum
181:    └ start marker (the only byte `ReadRecord` tests)
182: ```
183: 
184: Input reports are `0xFF`-padded to 65 bytes. `ReadCard` output is reproducible byte-for-byte
185: across reads, so the random nonce of §7.2 is stored on the card, not regenerated at read time.
186: 
187: ### 5.3 Write payload length is variable (**verified on hardware**)
188: 
189: `n` is not fixed at `0x21`: the reader accepts a **16-byte** payload for `cmd = 0xEC` as well.
190: 
191: | Frame | Total | Result |
192: |---|---|---|
193: | `AA 21 EC` + 32-byte payload + xor | 36 | accepted (`proRFL.WriteCard`) |
194: | `AA 11 EC` + 16-byte record + xor | 20 | **accepted — card read back the exact record** |
195: 
196: Both were sent to the same TEMIC card through `d12c.writePortPro(0x40, …)` and read back with
197: `ReadCard`:
198: 
199: ```
200: AA21EC C9121722FF00318000B919D2C029D5FB 00×16 72   → nonce 0x29 became 0x31 on the card
201: AA11EC C91224B6E3818101016265DB1565E300 B2          → guest record stored byte-for-byte
202: ```
203: 
204: So a rebuild only needs the compact form (`n = 0x11`); the reader still keeps a **20-byte card
205: area** (record + its own 4-byte trailer, §9 item 1), and the extra 16 bytes of the `0x21` form are
206: ignored.
207: 
208: ## 6. Card type selector — record byte 9 (**verified**)
209: 
210: Byte 9 (offset `0x3B` in the builder stack frame) is `type | (index & 0x0F)`:
211: 
212: | Byte 9 | Card |
213: |---|---|---|
214: | `0x10 + n` | `RecordCard` (lock record readout) |
215: | `0x20 + n` | `RoomSetCard` (assign room number to lock) |
216: | `0x30 + n` | `TimeSetCard` (set lock clock) |
217: | `0x40 + n` | `LimitCard` |
218: | `0x50 + n` | `GroupSetCard` |
219: | `0x60 + n` | `GuestCard` |
220: | `0x70 + n` | `CheckOutCard` |
221: | `0x80 + n` | `GroupCard` |
222: | `0xA0 + n` | `EmergencyCard` |
223: | `0xB0 + n` | `MasterCard` |
224: | `0xC0 + n` | `BuildingCard` (`(n & 0xF) - 0x40`) |
225: | `0xD0 + n` | `FloorCard` (`(n & 0xF) - 0x30`) |
226: 
227: `n` is the card sequence/index handed in by the caller.
228: 
229: **Cross-check against the installed database** (62 `CardInfo` rows): byte 9 values are
230: `0x60,0x61,0x62,0x69,0x6C,0x6F` (guest) and `0xB0…0xBF` (master) plus 16 rows in a different
231: layout (see §9). This matches the table above and confirms the mapping.
232:

234:

236: 
237: | Byte | Value |
238: |---|---|
239: | 0 | `0xC9` (magic) |

They are\n  used **only** as an oracle while building and testing the clone.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Source of truth\n\n| Question | Document |\n|---|---|\n| Stack, modules, data flow, activation | `ARCHITECTURE.md` |\n| Frames, checksums, transports, record bytes | `CARD-API.md` |\n| Encoder bring-up and harnesses | `ENCODER.md` |\n| Screens, widgets, event handlers | `FORMS.md` |\n| Tables, columns, SQL used by the EXE | `DATA-MODEL.md` |\n\n---\n\n## 2. Feature inventory (nothing omitted)\n\n### 2.1 Screens — 11 forms, 4 dialogs\n\n| Form | Role | Rebuild target |\n|---|---|---|\n| `frmLogon` | operator login | `LockLoginScreen` |\n| `frmMain` | shell, menu, toolbar | `LockShell` |\n| `frmReceiption` | check-in, check-out, card search, room state | `LockReceptionScreen` |\n| `frmKeysForStaff` | staff cards: floor, building, master, emergency, group, **record**, blacklist, check-out, issue | `LockStaffCardsScreen` |\n| `frmLockConfiguration` | per-lock parameters (alarm, remind, no-disturb, knob, music, cover…) | `LockConfigScreen` |\n| `frmRoomsDefination` | buildings, floors, rooms, lock addressing | `LockRoomsScreen` |\n| `frmReports` | occupancy, openings, guest history | `LockReportsScreen` |\n| `frmSystemMaintenance` | options, **System Registe** tab, operator management | `LockSettingsScreen` |\n| `LoginDialog` | DB login | inline dialog |\n| `PasswordDialog` | password entry / change | inline dialog |\n| `ProgressDialog` | progress | inline status |\n| `TData1`, `TData2`, `TDSSCubeEditor`, `TRzFrmCustomizeToolbar` | third-party/library artefacts | **not rebuilt** |\n\n### 2.2 Card types — 13\n\nSelector byte 9 = `0xTT | (index & 0x0F)`.\n\n| # | Type | `TT` | Vendor export | Status |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 0 | Reset | — | `ResetCard` | layout to transcribe |\n| 1 | Record (lock log) | `0x10` | `RecordCard` | **decoded** |\n| 2 | RoomSet | `0x20` | `RoomSetCard` | to transcribe |\n| 3 | TimeSet | `0x30` | `TimeSetCard` | to transcribe |\n| 4 | Limit | `0x40` | `LimitCard` | to transcribe |\n| 5 | GroupSet | `0x50` | `GroupSetCard` | to transcribe |\n| 6 | Guest | `0x60` | `GuestCard` | **decoded + hardware-verified** |\n| 7 | CheckOut | `0x70` | `CheckOutCard` | to transcribe |\n| 8 | Group | `0x80` | `GroupCard` | to transcribe |\n| 10 | Emergency | `0xA0` | `EmergencyCard` | to transcribe |\n| 11 | Master | `0xB0` | `MasterCard` | partially |\n| 12 | Building | `0xC0` | `BuildingCard` | to transcribe |\n| 13 | Floor | `0xD0` | `FloorCard` | to transcribe |\n\nWriter dispatcher: `FUN_006d8c44` (case = type). Builders captured in\n`proRFL.dll` at `0x10001005…0x100010a0` (decompiled dump kept outside the repo).\n\n### 2.3 Reader / communication operations — 26 exports\n\n`initializeUSB`, `Buzzer`, `CardErase`, `CloseCard`, `proTest`, `GetDLLVersion`,\n`ResetCard`, `RecordCard`, `RoomSetCard`, `TimeSetCard`, `LimitCard`, `GroupSetCard`,\n`GuestCard`, `CheckOutCard`, `GroupCard`, `EmergencyCard`, `MasterCard`, `BuildingCard`,\n`FloorCard`, `IniCard`, `IniCard1`, `ReadCard`, `WriteCard`, `ReadRecord`, `ReadE2`,\n`WriteE2`, plus helpers `a_hex`, `hex_a`.\n\n### 2.4 Data model — 10 tables\n\n`BuildingInfo`, `RoomInfo`, `GuestInfo`, `CardInfo`, `OperatorInfo`, `RecordOpen`,\n`RegInfo`, `LogInfo`, `CaoZuoInfo`, `Dai`.\n\nRebuild: SQLite schema with the same semantics; import from `CardLock.mdb` via a\none-shot migration (read-only, password from local config).\n\n### 2.5 Global options\n\n`System.ini [SYSTEM]`: hotel name, skin, `DBBakPath`, checkout times, VIP checkout,\nguest bolt, alarm, remind, no-disturb, knob, music, cover.\n\n---\n\n## 3. Target architecture\n\n```\nsrc/locks/\n  protocol/      frames, checksums, command builders, response parsing\n  transport/     LockTransport interface + webhid / capacitor-usb / windows-agent / mock\n  cards/         one module per card type + registry + decode/encode\n  reader/        high-level operations (issue, read, erase, log, memory)\n  domain/        rooms, guests, cards, records (pure, testable)\n  data/          sqlite/schema, mdb migration, repositories\n  ui/            screens, dialogs, i18n keys\n```\n\nRules\n\n- `protocol/` and `cards/` are **pure**: no DOM, no hardware, no React. Fully unit-tested.\n- Only `transport/` touches a device; swapping transport must not change upper layers.\n- Every user-facing string goes through the existing i18n mechanism (fr/en/ar).\n\nTransport options, in order of preference\n\n1. **WebHID** — the reader is a vendor-defined HID device (VID `0x9915`, PID `0x1116`).\n   Works in the browser and in the Windows WebView shell; no agent to install.\n2. **Capacitor USB host** — the Android build, same protocol over `UsbManager`.\n3. **Windows agent** — small local HTTP service wrapping the HID stack, as a fallback\n   for environments where WebHID is blocked.\n4. **Mock** — scripted responses for tests and CI.\n\n---\n\n## 4. Any mismatch is a bug on our side.\n2. **Hardware round trip** — write a record, read it back, compare 16 bytes\n   (`card-rw.ps1` does this already).\n3. **Lock acceptance** — a card is only \"correct\" when the lock accepts it (beeps,\n   opens, or writes its log).\n4. **Unit tests** — protocol/cards/domain are pure and must stay covered.\n\n## 6. ### frames.ts

```ts
export const FRAME_START = 0xaa;
export const RESPONSE_START = 0x55;

export function xorChecksum(bytes: readonly number[] | Uint8Array, from = 0, to = bytes.length): number
export function buildFrame(command: number, payload: readonly number[] = []): Uint8Array
export interface LockResponse { raw, status, data, checksumOk }
export function parseResponse(bytes: Uint8Array): LockResponse
export function tryParseResponse(bytes): LockResponse | null  // validates start + length + checksum
export function toHex(bytes): string
export function fromHex(hex): Uint8Array
```

Frame: `AA <n> <cmd> <n-1 bytes> <xor>`, n = 1 + payload.length, checksum = XOR of all preceding bytes (including AA). Verified: `ReadCard AA 01 E4 4F`: XOR(AA,01,E4) = AA^01 = AB; AB^E4 = 4F. ✓

`Buzzer AA 02 80 <lvl> <lvl^0x28>`: XOR(AA,02,80,lvl) = (AA^02)=A8 ^80 = 28 ^ lvl. Yes = lvl^0x28. ✓

Response: `55 <n> <status> <data n-1> <xor>`; xor over preceding bytes. Check ReadE2 response `55 21 01` + 32 bytes + xor: n=0x21=33, data = 32 = n-1. ✓ total length = 3 + (n-1) + 1 = n+3 = 36.

So `parseResponse` expects `bytes.length === n + 3`.

Write frame: `AA 11 EC` + 16 + xor → n = 0x11 = 17 = 1 + 16. ✓

  "content": "/**\n * proUSB reader frame grammar.\n *\n * The encoder is a vendor-defined HID device (VID 0x9915 / PID 0x1116) that\n * speaks a tiny binary protocol over 65-byte reports.\n *\n * Command frame\n *   AA | n | cmd | payload[n-1] | xor\n *   n         = payload.length + 1\n *   xor       = XOR of every preceding byte\n *\n * Response frame\n *   55 | n | status | data[n-1] | xor\n *   n         = data.length + 1\n *   xor       = XOR of every preceding byte\n *\n * The reader pads reports with 0xFF, so a response is always read from the\n * declared length and never from the transport buffer size.\n *\n * Reference: docs/re-proUSB/CARD-API.md §5 and §6.\n *\n * This module is pure: no DOM, no hardware, no React. It must stay testable\n * in Node and safe to import anywhere.\n */\n\n/** First byte of every host-to-reader frame. */\nexport const FRAME_START = 0xaa;\n\n/** First byte of every reader-to-host frame. */\nexport const RESPONSE_START = 0x55;\n\n/** Largest frame accepted by the reader (one 64-byte HID report + marker). */\nexport const MAX_PAYLOAD = 0xff - 1;\n\n/** A response that cannot be decoded into a valid frame. */\nexport class FrameError extends Error {\n  constructor(message: string) {\n    super(message);\n    this.name = 'FrameError';\n  }\n}\n\n/** A response whose checksum does not match its content. */\nexport class ChecksumError extends FrameError {\n  readonly expected: number;\n  readonly actual: number;\n\n  constructor(expected: number, actual: number) {\n    super(`checksum mismatch: expected 0x${hex(expected)}, got 0x${hex(actual)}`);\n    this.name = 'ChecksumError';\n    this.expected = expected;\n    this.actual = actual;\n  }\n}\n\n/** XOR of `bytes[from, to)`. This is the only checksum the reader uses. */\nexport function xorChecksum(bytes: ArrayLike<number>, from = 0, to = bytes.length): number {\n  let value = 0;\n  for (let i = from; i < to; i += 1) value ^= bytes[i] & 0xff;\n  return value & 0xff;\n}\n\n/**\n * Build a host-to-reader frame.\n *\n * `buildFrame(0xe4)` -> `AA 01 E4 4F` (ReadCard, verified on hardware).\n * `buildFrame(0x80, [0x01])` -> `AA 02 80 01 29` (Buzzer on).\n */\nexport function buildFrame(command: number, payload: readonly number[] = []): Uint8Array {\n  assertByte(command, 'command');\n  if (payload.length > MAX_PAYLOAD) {\n    throw new RangeError(`payload too long: ${payload.length} > ${MAX_PAYLOAD}`);\n  }\n  for (const byte of payload) assertByte(byte, 'payload');\n\n  const length = payload.length + 1;\n  const frame = new Uint8Array(length + 3);\n  frame[0] = FRAME_START;\n  frame[1] = length;\n  frame[2] = command;\n  frame.set(payload, 3);\n  frame[frame.length - 1] = xorChecksum(frame, 0, frame.length - 1);\n  return frame;\n}\n\n/** A decoded reader response. */\nexport interface LockResponse {\n  /** Status byte sent by the reader (`0x01` = accepted). */\n  status: number;\n  /** Response payload, `n - 1` bytes. */\n  data: Uint8Array;\n  /** Declared payload length + 1 (`n`). */\n  length: number;\n  /** Number of bytes consumed from the buffer, padding excluded. */\n  frameLength: number;\n  /** Full frame as received, checksum included. */\n  raw: Uint8Array;\n}\n\n/**\n * Decode a response buffer.\n *\n * Trailing 0xFF padding is ignored. Throws {@link FrameError} when the buffer\n * cannot hold a complete frame and {@link ChecksumError} when the checksum is\n * wrong, so a corrupted read never reaches a card codec.\n */\nexport function parseResponse(bytes: Uint8Array): LockResponse {\n  if (bytes.length < 4) {\n    throw new FrameError(`response too short: ${bytes.length} byte(s)`);\n  }\n  if (bytes[0] !== RESPONSE_START) {\n    throw new FrameError(`bad start byte: 0x${hex(bytes[0])} (expected 0x55)`);\n  }\n\n  const length = bytes[1];\n  if (length < 1) throw new FrameError(`bad length byte: 0x${hex(length)}`);\n\n  const frameLength = length + 3;\n  if (bytes.length < frameLength) {\n    throw new FrameError(`truncated frame: need ${frameLength}, got ${bytes.length}`);\n  }\n\n  const expected = xorChecksum(bytes, 0, frameLength - 1);\n  const actual = bytes[frameLength - 1];\n  if (expected !== actual) throw new ChecksumError(expected, actual);\n\n  return {\n    status: bytes[2],\n    data: bytes.slice(3, frameLength - 1),\n    length,\n    frameLength,\n    raw: bytes.slice(0, frameLength),\n  };\n}\n\n/** `parseResponse` but returns `null` instead of throwing. */\nexport function tryParseResponse(bytes: Uint8Array): LockResponse | null {\n  try {\n    return parseResponse(bytes);\n  } catch {\n    return null;\n  }\n}\n\n/** True when the reader accepted the command. */\nexport function isAccepted(response: LockResponse): boolean {\n  return response.status === 0x01;\n}\n\n/** Lowercase hex, no separators. `Uint8Array.of(0xaa, 0x01)` -> `\"aa01\"`. */\nexport function toHex(bytes: ArrayLike<number>): string {\n  let out = '';\n  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) out += (bytes[i] & 0xff).toString(16).padStart(2, '0');\n  return out;\n}\n\n/** Parse hex, ignoring spaces and separators. Throws on odd length or bad digits. */\nexport function fromHex(text: string): Uint8Array {\n  const clean = text.replace(/[\\s:_-]/g, '').toLowerCase();\n  if (clean.length % 2 !== 0) throw new FrameError(`odd hex length: ${clean.length}`);\n  if (!/^[0-9a-f]*$/.test(clean)) throw new FrameError('invalid hex digit');\n  const out = new Uint8Array(clean.length / 2);\n  for (let i = 0; i < out.length; i += 1) out[i] = parseInt(clean.slice(i * 2, i * 2 + 2), 16);\n  return out;\n}\n\nfunction hex(value: number): string {\n  return (value & 0xff).toString(16).padStart(2, '0');\n}\n\nfunction assertByte(value: number, label: string): void {\n  if (!Number.isInteger(value) || value < 0 || value > 0xff) {\n    throw new RangeError(`${label} out of range: ${value}`);\n  }\n}\n"

Everything above it (frames, commands, card\n * codecs, domain logic) is transport-agnostic, so the same code runs over\n * WebHID, Android USB host, a local Windows agent, or the mock used in tests.\n *\n * Known hardware behaviour that the retry policy exists for:\n * - the reader re-enumerates intermittently (~1 probe in 3 misses);\n * - `cmd = 0xEC` (WriteCard) never sends a reply;\n * - some reads block for ~2 s and then return zeros.\n *\n * Reference: docs/re-proUSB/ENCODER.md §3 and CARD-API.md §5.\n */\n\nimport { type LockResponse, parseResponse } from './frames.ts';\n\n/** The device could not be opened, was lost, or refused the transfer. */\nexport class TransportError extends Error {\n  constructor(message: string, options?: { cause?: unknown }) {\n    super(message, options);\n    this.name = 'TransportError';\n  }\n}\n\n/** No complete response arrived before the deadline. */\nexport class LockTimeoutError extends TransportError {\n  constructor(timeoutMs: number) {\n    super(`no response from the encoder within ${timeoutMs} ms`);\n    this.name = 'LockTimeoutError';\n  }\n}\n\n/** The reader answered, but with a non-zero status byte. */\nexport class LockStatusError extends Error {\n  readonly status: number;\n\n  constructor(status: number) {\n    super(`reader rejected the command with status 0x${status.toString(16).padStart(2, '0')}`);\n    this.name = 'LockStatusError';\n    this.status = status;\n  }\n}\n\n/**\n * Minimal byte pipe to a card reader.\n *\n * Implementations must be safe to call `open()` twice and `close()` when not\n * open; the reader layer relies on that to recover from a lost device.\n */\nexport interface LockTransport {\n  /** Stable identifier, useful in logs (`webhid`, `usb`, `agent`, `mock`). */\n  readonly id: string;\n  open(): Promise<void>;\n  close(): Promise<void>;\n  /** Send one host frame. May resolve before the device has processed it. */\n  send(frame: Uint8Array): Promise<void>;\n  /** Wait for one reader frame. Returns `null` on timeout instead of throwing. */\n  receive(timeoutMs: number): Promise<Uint8Array | null>;\n}\n\nexport interface TransactOptions {\n  /** Deadline for a single response. Defaults to 2000 ms (hardware measured). */\n  timeoutMs?: number;\n  /** Total attempts on timeout or corruption. Defaults to 3. */\n  attempts?: number;\n  /** Delay between attempts. Defaults to 120 ms. */\n  retryDelayMs?: number;\n}\n\n/**\n * Send a frame and decode the response, retrying the whole exchange.\n *\n * Retrying the exchange (not the receive) is deliberate: the reader only\n * answers the first read after a command, so a half-consumed response must be\n * flushed by issuing the command again.\n */\nexport async function transact(\n  transport: LockTransport,\n  frame: Uint8Array,\n  options: TransactOptions = {},\n): Promise<LockResponse> {\n  const timeoutMs = options.timeoutMs ?? 2000;\n  const attempts = Math.max(1, options.attempts ?? 3);\n  const retryDelayMs = options.retryDelayMs ?? 120;\n\n  let lastError: unknown = null;\n\n  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1) {\n    await transport.send(frame);\n    const received = await transport.receive(timeoutMs);\n\n    if (received) {\n      try {\n        return parseResponse(received);\n      } catch (error) {\n        lastError = error;\n      }\n    } else {\n      lastError = new LockTimeoutError(timeoutMs);\n    }\n\n    if (attempt < attempts) await sleep(retryDelayMs);\n  }\n\n  throw lastError instanceof Error ? lastError : new TransportError('exchange failed');\n}\n\n/**\n * Scriptable in-memory transport.\n *\n * Used by the unit tests and by the UI when no encoder is plugged in, so every\n * screen can be exercised without hardware.\n */\nexport class MockTransport implements LockTransport {\n  readonly id = 'mock';\n  /** Every frame the caller sent, in order. Useful in tests. */\n  readonly sent: Uint8Array[] = [];\n  private opened = false;\n  private responder: (frame: Uint8Array) => Uint8Array | null | Promise<Uint8Array | null>;\n\n  constructor(responder: (frame: Uint8Array) => Uint8Array | null | Promise<Uint8Array | null>) {\n    this.responder = responder;\n  }\n\n  /** Replace the behaviour without recreating the transport. */\n  respondWith(responder: (frame: Uint8Array) => Uint8Array | null | Promise<Uint8Array | null>): void {\n    this.responder = responder;\n  }\n\n  get isOpen(): boolean {\n    return this.opened;\n  }\n\n  async open(): Promise<void> {\n    this.opened = true;\n  }\n\n  async close(): Promise<void> {\n    this.opened = false;\n  }\n\n  async send(frame: Uint8Array): Promise<void> {\n    if (!this.opened) throw new TransportError('transport is not open');\n    this.sent.push(frame.slice());\n  }\n\n  async receive(): Promise<Uint8Array | null> {\n    const frame = this.sent[this.sent.length - 1];\n    if (!frame) return null;\n    return this.responder(frame);\n  }\n}\n\nfunction sleep(ms: number): Promise<void> {\n  return new Promise((resolve) => {\n    setTimeout(resolve, ms);\n  });\n}\n",

=== lock-log.ps1 head ===
<#
.SYNOPSIS
    Issues a "Record Card" for a proUSB/TEMIC lock and reads the lock event log back.

.DESCRIPTION
    The vendor software never talks to a lock directly. It uses a *record card*:

        1. the software writes a record card  (proRFL.RecordCard, type byte 0x10|n)
        2. the card is inserted in the lock   (the lock appends its event log to it)
        3. the card comes back to the reader  (proRFL.ReadRecord, frame AA 01 82 29)
        4. the log is stored in CardLock.mdb / RecordOpen

    Step 1 and 3 are reproduced here from the vendor DLL, so a card can be issued and
    read without the vendor application.

    The reader is reached through d12c.dll (x86), therefore this script must run under
    32-bit PowerShell:
        %WINDIR%\SysWOW64\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -File lock-log.ps1 ...

    Only for cards and locks you own or administer.
